map.铁过载（血清铁蛋白）评估器 使用指南: Iron Overload (Serum Ferritin) Assessor User Guide
map.铁过载（血清铁蛋白）评估器。输入血清铁蛋白值与基础疾病，评估铁过载程度并给出祛铁: Iron overload (serum ferritin) assessor. Enter the serum ferritin value and the underlying disease to grade iron overload and suggest an iron removal treatment strategy, as a reference for iron metabolism management in hematology.
map.输血依赖患者按铁蛋白定铁过载程度与祛铁时机: For transfusion-dependent patients, grade the iron overload and the timing of iron removal by ferritin
map.按基础病选祛铁方案（地拉罗司/去铁胺/放血）: Choose an iron removal plan by underlying disease (deferasirox / deferoxamine / phlebotomy)
map.评估年输铁量，指导监测频率: Assess annual iron intake to guide monitoring frequency
map.：铁蛋白分级：<500 无、500–999 轻度、1000–2499 中度、25: : Ferritin grading: <500 none, 500-999 mild, 1000-2499 moderate, 2500-4999 severe, >=5000 extremely severe. Iron removal (transfusion-dependent): deferasirox 20-40 mg/kg/day (thalassemia), MDS starting at a low dose of 5-20; phlebotomy is the first choice for hereditary hemochromatosis. Annual iron intake is about the transfusion count x 200 mg (each unit of red cells contains about 200 mg of iron).
map.：例（铁蛋白=2500、地贫、年输血 12 次）：分级=重度铁过载；地拉罗司剂量: : Example (ferritin = 2500, thalassemia, 12 transfusions per year): grade = severe iron overload; deferasirox dose = 2500/500, about 5.0, but the lower bound of 20 mg/kg/day is used (the 20-40 range); annual iron intake = 12x200 = 2400 mg, so iron overload progresses fast - check ferritin every 1-3 months and add cardiac MRI T2* when it reaches 2500 or more.
map.铁蛋白正常就无铁过载吗？: Does a normal ferritin rule out iron overload?
map.不一定。铁蛋白受炎症、肝病、肿瘤升高而假性增高；炎性活动期即使真实铁负荷高，铁蛋: Not necessarily. Ferritin rises falsely with inflammation, liver disease and tumors; even when true iron burden is high, ferritin may read "normal" during active inflammation. When needed, check transferrin saturation (TSAT) or liver/cardiac MRI T2* quantification.
map.为什么地贫地拉罗司 20–40 而 MDS 更低？: Why is deferasirox 20-40 for thalassemia but lower for MDS?
map.MDS 患者骨髓增生异常、感染/炎症常见，铁蛋白基线易偏高且耐受性差，故起始低剂: MDS patients commonly have myelodysplasia and infection or inflammation, with a baseline ferritin that tends to be high and poor tolerance, so start at a low dose (5-20) and titrate slowly; thalassemia patients are usually younger and tolerate well, so the standard 20-40 can be used.
